title: Conduct a cautious exploratory analysis
description: Inspect structure, missingness, distributions and relationships before modelling.
accomplishes: Inspect structure, missingness, distributions and relationships before modelling. Separate descriptive observations from causal interpretations. Propose useful plots and reproducible checks, flag sample limitations and avoid inventing statistics when values are unavailable.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Conduct a cautious exploratory analysis.

Input context:
- DATA: [DATA]
- DICTIONARY: [DICTIONARY]
- QUESTION: [QUESTION]
- LIMITS: [LIMITS]

Inspect structure, missingness, distributions and relationships before modelling. Separate descriptive observations from causal interpretations. Propose useful plots and reproducible checks, flag sample limitations and avoid inventing statistics when values are unavailable.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Exploration outline
Start with row counts, field types and missing values, then inspect relevant distributions by the supplied grouping. Check whether repeated entities distort summaries. A relationship between enquiries and spend is not proof of causation. Without actual data, the output remains an analysis plan and must not contain fabricated averages or correlations.
